case_title: Virendra Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute: the accused's family demanded that the victim reap their crop and became annoyed when he refused; no kinship stated
weapon: Firearm (pistol/rifle) fired by a co-accused; the appellant was armed with a lathi
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (injured eyewitness and other witnesses), including the injured son, another son and a daughter of the victim
aggravating_circumstances: Accused went armed to teach the victim a lesson; prearranged plan; victim was shot after intervening to protect his son
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 read with s.34 IPC; sentence not stated
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 262 of 1986) dismissed; conviction under s.302 read with s.34 upheld
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 read with s.34
neutral_facts: The victim was asked by the accused and two family members to reap the accused's family's crop the next day. The victim replied that he was busy with his own harvest and with family ceremonies planned in the coming days, but the accused persons pressed him to reap the crop. The victim refused, and the accused's family became annoyed. The next morning at about 7 a.m., the accused and two others went to the victim's house. The accused and one companion were armed with lathis and the third was armed with a rifle. They asked the victim why he had not gone to reap the crop. After the victim repeated his refusal, the accused and a companion began abusing and beating the victim's son with lathis. Other family members, including the victim's mother, sister, another son and a relative, rushed to protect the son and were also struck with lathis and injured. The victim then intervened. One of the companions was told to shoot the victim, and fired a shot that struck the victim in the stomach, causing death. The same person also fired at the victim's son but the pellets missed him. Pellets injured another son and the daughter. After the shooting, the group ran away towards a canal. The incident was witnessed by two persons. An injured eyewitness, another son and the daughter gave detailed accounts describing the role of the accused in beating the family members and the shooting.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a gunshot wound to the stomach; the victim's son, another son, daughter and mother injured by lathi blows, a fracture of the mother's hand and pellet injuries
premeditation_planning: Court found a prearranged plan and prior meeting of minds: the three went armed to the victim's house to teach him a lesson
motive: Court accepted: to teach the victim a lesson for refusing to reap the accused's crop (revenge for disobeying their orders)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness accounts of the injured eyewitness, another son and the daughter about the beating, the exhortation and the shooting; the Court relied on the conduct of the group arriving armed
witness_credibility: Courts below found the prosecution witnesses consistent and not shaken in cross-examination; the Supreme Court recorded this without separate criticism
post_offence_conduct: Fled towards the canal after the shooting
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 17.5.2002; Supreme Court: 09.08.2010
legal_representation: Appellant: D.B. Vohra, T. Hashmi, S.K. Sabharwal. State (Respondent): Siddharth Dave, Vibha Datta Makhija
investigation_status: Not stated (investigation details not described; trial completed with conviction)
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 read with s.34 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: The appellant is vicariously liable under s.302 read with s.34 IPC for the shooting by a co-accused, given the prearranged plan and that all three were armed
defence_argument: Section 34 IPC could not be invoked against the appellant, since the fatal shot was fired by a co-accused and the appellant's own acts did not amount to the murder
legal_principle_applied: Section 34 requires common intention (prearranged plan or meeting of minds, anterior to the crime) and actual participation in the crime; distinguished from s.149
precedent_relied_upon: Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. King Emperor AIR 1925 PC 1; Mehbub Shah v. King-Emperor AIR 1945 PC 148; Pandurang v. State of Hyderabad (1955) 1 SCR 1083; Mohan Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1963 SC 174; Ramaswami Ayyangar (1976) 3 SCC 779; Surendra Chauhan (2000) 4 SCC 110; Amrik Singh 1972 CrLJ 465 (SC); and others
judicial_aggravating_factors: No grave or sudden provocation; prearranged plan to teach the victim a lesson while armed
